rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joined names such as Ḥaḍramawt and Baʿlabakk can be treated as compounds, while some Arabs instead construe parts such as Baʿl as an iḍāfa.
rows.anchor: وذلك نحو حضرموت وبعلبك ومن العرب من يضيف بعل إلى بك

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: Arabic speakers vary over Maʿd Yakrib: some use iḍāfa, others make it one name, and some treat Yakrib as feminine and leave the form uninflected.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يقول معد يكرب فيضيف

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus explains that native two-part personal names resist declension because their joined structure is not an original noun pattern; Maʿd Yakrib remains declinable when indefinite.
rows.anchor: فقلت ليونس هلا صرفوه إذ جعلوه اسما واحدا وهو عربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fifteen and its forms combine two numerals as one word; ḥādī ʿashar is also made indeclinable, likened to the ambiguous demonstrative أولاء, and does not take nunation.
rows.anchor: فهما شيئان جعلا شيئا واحدا وإنما أصل خمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حيص بيص is another uninflected expression treated as a single unit; Umayya's verse supplies an example.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا في كلامهم حيص بيص مفتوحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because it is frequent and indefinite, خمسة عشر stays unchanged with iḍāfa or the article; the variant خمسة عشرك is judged poor.
rows.anchor: تدع خمسة عشر في الإضافة والألف واللام على حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الخازباز means either a garden fly or a disease; speakers vary in its form, including الخزباز, which some treat like سربال and attest in poetry.
rows.anchor: وهو عند بعضهم الداء جعلوا لفظه كلفظ نظائره

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb heard حي هل الصلاة; حيهل combines حي على الصلاة, and a poem's joined form supports treating it as one name.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو الخطاب أنه سمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When these compounds become proper names, they are inflected and altered like Ḥaḍramawt; demonstratives, من, sounds, and لو likewise change when used as particles.
rows.anchor: وجميع هذا إذا صار شيء منه

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: Arabic forms of حيهل vary in connected speech and pause, including whether the final alif is retained; الخازباز also has compound variants.
rows.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول حيهلا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl regards عمرويه as foreign but specially altered: definite عمرويه is indeclinable, while the indefinite form takes tanwin with kasra.
rows.anchor: وعمرويه عندهم بمنزلة حضرموت في أنه ضم الآخر

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says speakers who omit tanwin on sounds such as غاق and عاء treat them as definite; speakers who add it treat them as indefinite.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن الذين يقولون غاق غاق وعاء وحاء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes صه, هيهات, إيه, and related forms as indefinite sound-words, including their distinct pause forms.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن الذين قالوا صه ذاك أرادوا النكرة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl treats فداء لك like أمس because of frequency; genitive is lighter in its common use, and it is nunated as an indefinite.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن قوله فداء لك فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paired expressions such as يوم يوم and ابن عم / ابن أم are pronounced as one word only in adverbial, circumstantial, or vocative use; otherwise the base construction is iḍāfa.
rows.anchor: يا ابن عم ويا ابن أم بمنزلة شيء واحد إلا في حال النداء

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus reports that Abū ʿAmr pronounced reduplicated expressions as one word in adverbial or circumstantial use; the author says iḍāfa is the regular analysis and cites al-Farazdaq.
rows.anchor: وزعم يونس وهو رأيه أن أبا عمر و كان يجعل لفظه

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus cites Ruʾba's كفة عن كفة to show the second element is genitive and the expression remains an iḍāfa in this adverbial use.
rows.anchor: أن يونس زعم أن رؤبة كان يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيادي سبا, قالي قلا, and بادي بدا are generally joined like خمسة عشر, though some construe سبا in iḍāfa and nunate it, as in Dhū al-Rumma's verse.
rows.anchor: وأما أيادي سبا وقالي قلا وبادي بدا فإنما هي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بادي بدا is treated like خمسة عشر; the author has not heard it in iḍāfa, though he allows that construction, and reports بادي بدي.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله كان ذلك بادي بدا فإنهم جعلوها بمنزلة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl explains that yāʾ endings in joined names stay uninflected like dual alif, since they are internal to the compound rather than case endings; poets attest their forms.
rows.anchor: الخليل عن الياءات لم لم تنصب في موضع النصب

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl distinguishes اثنا عشر from خمسة عشر: case appears on اثنا / اثني, عشر behaves like nunation, and عشر is deleted if the expression becomes a personal name.
rows.anchor: فزعم الخليل أنه لا يغير عن حاله قبل التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخول أخول may belong either with the joined expressions شغر بغر or with the adverbial يوم يوم pattern.
rows.anchor: وأما أخول أخول فلا يخلوا من أن يكون كشغر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some nouns denote a collective without being broken plurals of a singular; ركب and سفر show this because their diminutives are ركيب and سفير, not restored singular forms.
rows.anchor: فالركب لم يكسر عليه راكب ألا ترى أنك تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طير and صحب likewise are collective forms rather than broken plurals of طائر and صاحب.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك طائر وطير وصاحب وصحب

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl classifies الكمأة and الجبأة as collective nouns, not plurals of كم; the diminutive كميئة supports the analysis.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن مثل ~~ذلك الكمأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أدم is a collective corresponding to أديم, alongside أفق / أفيق and عمد / عمود.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك أديم وأدم والدليل

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus reports the masculine usage هو العمد for the collective عمد.
rows.anchor: وقال ~~يونس يقولون هو العمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حلق and فلك are not broken plurals of حلقة and فلكة; the author contrasts them with a genuine broken plural such as ظلم from ظلمة.
rows.anchor: حلقة كما كسروا ظلمة على ظلم

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports نشفة / نشف for the stone used for rubbing oneself.
rows.anchor: فيما حدثنا أبو الخطاب نشفة ونشف وهو الحجر الذي يتدلك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الجامل and الباقر are collective nouns, not broken plurals of جمل and بقرة; masculine agreement and diminutive formation are evidence.
rows.anchor: الباقر لم يكسر عليهما جمل ولا بقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms أخ / إخوة and سري / سراة are not ordinary broken plurals; سروات and weak-root analogues support this distinction.
rows.anchor: أخ وإخوة وسري وسراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاره and فرهة pattern like صاحب and صحبة, just as راكب and ركب do.
rows.anchor: وقد قالوا فاره وفرهة مثل صاحب وصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غيب and خدم are collectives like أدم; related pairs include أهب, معز, ضأن, عزيب, and غزي, with Imruʾ al-Qays's verse witnessing غزي.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك غائب وغيب وخادم وخدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a name ending in tāʾ marbūṭa is treated after truncation as a name without it, عرقوة and قمحدوة yield عرقى and قمحدى.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك في عرقوة وقمحدوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same truncation analysis gives يا رعى from رعوم and يا قطا from قطوان.
rows.anchor: وكذلك إن رخمت رعوم وجعلته بهذه المنزلة قلت يا رعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طفاوة becomes يا طفاء when the remainder is treated as a name without tāʾ, because the language has no noun with that final pattern.
rows.anchor: يا طفاء أقبل من قبل أنه ليس في الكلام اسم هكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the remaining wāw is not made an inflectional ending, it stays unchanged after truncating طفاوة: يا طفاو.
rows.anchor: فهي على حالها قبل أن تحذف الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating the remainder as a noun without tāʾ is less common; speakers more often preserve its form because case endings elsewhere change.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ما يجعل بمنزلة اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truncation يا معا from معاوية is supported by al-ʿAjjāj's verse, showing that this treatment is native Arabic.
rows.anchor: قد حملهم ذلك على أن رخموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حيوة becomes يا حيو; in the nominative its wāw remains by the original pattern غزو, so the change is not obligatory.
rows.anchor: وتقول في حيوة يا حيو أقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may not drop tāʾ and treat the remainder as masculine for an ordinary feminine noun, since that would confuse gender; the exception is a dominant proper name.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لا يجوز أن تحذف الهاء وتجعل البقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truncation of names not ending in tāʾ is less common because it removes both tanwin and an inherent final consonant, though it is permitted.
rows.anchor: أن لا يحذف منها أكثر لأنهم كرهوا أن يخلوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names such as حارث, مالك, and عامر are especially often shortened because they are frequent personal names and common in poetry; several poets attest them.
rows.anchor: وليس الحذف لشئ من هذه الأسماء ألزم منه لحارث ومالك وعامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any proper name may be shortened in address; examples include يزيد as يزى, ليلى as ليل, and لميس as لمى.
rows.anchor: وكل اسم خاص رخمته في النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's verse uses طريف بن مال for طريف بن مالك, showing a name without tāʾ may also be shortened in poetry.
rows.anchor: طريف بن مال ليلة الجوع والخصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text cites a line attributed to Ṭarafa as a constructed example by an ʿĀbidī poet, with سعد shortened from أسعد.
rows.anchor: مصنوع على طرفة وهو لبعض العباديين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports al-Khalīl's rule that names are shortened from five letters to four and four to three, with three-letter names as the lower limit.
rows.anchor: وكان غاية التخفيف عندهم لأنه أخف شئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only dominant proper names without tāʾ are normally shortened, since they are frequent enough to undergo deletion even outside address, as in زيد بن عمرو.
rows.anchor: ليس من اسم لا تكون في آخره هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا صاح for صاحب is an exceptional shortening justified by frequent use, like the conventional reductions لم أبل, لم يك, and لا أدر.
rows.anchor: إلا أنهم قد قالوا يا صاح وهم يريدون يا صاحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative من can mark number like أي: forms include منين for two or males, منه for a woman, منتين for two women, and منات for women plural.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنك تثنى من إذا قلت رأيت رجلين كما تثنى أيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In singular oblique contexts من has forms منو and مني, while أي behaves like fully declinable names in pause because it takes tanwin in the relative construction.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الواحد يخالف أيا في موضع الجر والرفع

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says the nūn in the forms of من is silent in connected speech; من يا فتى shows this relative construction.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أن

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl adduces منو in pause followed by من يا فتى to show the connected form works like من قال ذاك and can refer to a group.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أن الدليل على ذلك أنك تقول منو في الوقف ثم تقول من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أي can be pluralized, dualized, and added in the relative construction, whereas interrogative من does none of these; أي is stronger because it also takes tanwin and iḍāfa.
rows.anchor: وأي منون على كل حال في الاستفهام وغيره فهو أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh records Yūnus's report that some speakers keep من forms unchanged in pause regardless of number.
rows.anchor: منا ومني ومنو عنيت واحدا أو اثنين أو جميعا في الوقف

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus proposes منه analogized on أية as منة, but Sībawayh calls this distant and says it was heard only once in poetry.
rows.anchor: وأما يونس فإنه [ كان ] يقيس منه على أية

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus says he heard a Bedouin say ضرب من منا, then acknowledged not everyone accepted the form.
rows.anchor: وكان يونس إذا ذكرها يقول لا يقبل هذا كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh rejects the form as distant and says it is not widely used by Arabs.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد لا تكلم به العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asking about a woman and man, the first-mentioned gender determines whether the form is من / منا or من / منه.
rows.anchor: فبدأت في المسألة بالمؤنث قلت من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أي is pluralized in interrogative use because that is its main and original use; it behaves there like a complete noun, while من only partly parallels it.
rows.anchor: وإنما جمعت أي في الاستفهام
